dedupe_keys.name: dmi klimaatlas danish climate atlas of projected climate change by municipality

description: Klimaatlas is prepared by the National Centre for Climate Research at the Danish Meteorological Institute and holds data on expected future climate change at municipal level for the whole of Denmark, as a common evidence base that municipalities can use to plan climate adaptation. It covers temperature, precipitation, sea level and storm surge in the projected Danish climate, including how much temperature and sea level will rise and how precipitation, storm surge heights and the number of cloudbursts will change; headline figures on the page include 1.0 to 3.4 degrees of warming, 1.5 to 4.5 times more heat wave days, 30 to 50 centimetres of sea level rise and storm surges 9 to 20 times more frequent. Data is available for all of Denmark, municipalities, river catchments and coastal stretches, and can be downloaded in several file formats, as PDF reports and through a GIS service, with documentation on how the data was made, user cases and teaching material. Access is free; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: values are scenario ranges with uncertainty, and the pages are mainly in Danish. Coverage is Denmark. It supports climate adaptation and hazard exposure analysis for infrastructure, such as cloudburst, storm surge and heat planning; the related record is the Copenhagen cloudburst management plan case study.
